statements.statement: Chapter 70 funds increased $135,915 in the FY27 final budget versus the governor's proposal
Smart growth school reimbursement increased, as heard, $160,187,000
Total increase across all cherry sheet receipts (chapter 70, charter tuition reimbursement, smart growth, school choice, UGGA, elderly aid) is $491,988
State assessments/charges to the town (school choice and charter school sending tuition) rose a subtotal of $15,326
Net additional aid from the state, after subtracting the $15,326 in extra assessments from the $491,988 receipts increase, is $476,662
Legislature funded Lunenburg schools $418,000 above the governor's proposal; superintendent has a spending proposal for it
Argument raised for requesting the full $475,000 the town received above the governor's budget as a whole, not just the education portion
The school committee cut over $800,000 from its budget this year
An additional over $300,000 in one-time state budget money exists but is not being requested here
The town has over $9 million in its stabilization account; none of it is being asked for in this request

As voted at the prior meeting, the warrant article sought an additional $350,000 for the FY27 school operating budget
Governor Healey signed the FY27 state budget making available $418,056 more in education-specific receipts than the town's FY27 budget initially anticipated
School committee voted to amend its warrant article to request $418,056 for the FY27 school operating budget, to go before the extra special town meeting on September 3rd
Governor Healey has proposed an additional $100 million statewide from the millionaire's tax for schools via a per-pupil formula, pending the legislature
